'''Danny Granger Jr.''' (born April 20, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played ten seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was drafted by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2005 after a two-year college stint at [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]]. In 2009, Granger averaged 26 points per game on 45 percent shooting and was named an [[List of NBA All-Stars|All-Star]] and the league's [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]]. An injury to his left knee limited Granger to just five games during the 2012–13 season, and in February 2014, he was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He went on to play for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Miami Heat]] before having short stints with the [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Detroit Pistons]] in 2015.

==High school career==
Granger attended [[Grace King High School]] in [[Metairie, Louisiana]]. A four-year letterman at Grace King, he averaged 24.3 points, 12 rebounds and 5.5 blocks per game as a senior.<ref name=nbabio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/danny_granger/bio/ |title=Danny Granger Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425174227/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/danny_granger/bio/ |archive-date=April 25, 2015}}</ref> He was a [[McDonald's All-American]] nominee before his senior year.<ref name=abqjournal>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Mark|url=https://www.abqjournal.com/sports/426478sports01-21-06.htm|title=Ex-Lobo Danny Granger Wouldn't Have Career Any Other Way|work=abqjournal.com|date=January 21, 2006|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref> He scored a 30 on his [[ACT (test)|ACT]] and was accepted to [[Yale University]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Broussard|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?id=4018165|title=What's The Difference Between Danny Granger and Kobe Bryant?|work=ESPN.com|date=March 28, 2009|access-date=December 3, 2017|quote=The guy who scored an impressive 30 on his ACT and was accepted to Yale works on stuff some players don't even think about.}}</ref> Granger ultimately chose to attend and play [[college basketball]] at [[Bradley University]] in order to study [[Civil Engineering]], which was not offered at Yale.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://lasportshall.com/2025/06/23/granger-sparkled-at-every-level-by-doing-things-the-right-way-in-every-aspect/| title=Granger Sparkled at Every Level by Doing Things the Right Way in Every Aspect| website=lasportshall.com| first=Bill| last=Bumgarner| date=June 23, 2025| access-date=March 10, 2026}}</ref>

==College career==
===Bradley (2001–2003)===
Granger made the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] All-Freshman team for [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]] in 2001–02, averaging 11.1 points and 7.1 rebounds a game. 

He transferred to [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]] after the first semester of his sophomore season, having averaged 19.2 points and 7.9 rebounds for the Braves.<ref name="abqjournal" /> He said the reason for the transfer was because of Bradley head coach [[Jim Les]]'s intimidating tactics,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1526721|title=Bradley University committee rejects Granger's appeal|publisher=ESPN|date=March 20, 2003|access-date=March 20, 2003}}</ref> including being "verbally abusive."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1518186|title=Granger says New Mexico didn't recruit him|publisher=ESPN|date=March 4, 2003|access-date=March 4, 2003}}</ref>

===New Mexico (2003–2005)===
====Junior====
Granger wasn't eligible to start playing for the Lobos until January 2004,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1498476|title=Bradley contends tampering involved in transfer|publisher=ESPN|date=January 25, 2003|access-date=January 25, 2003}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1577853|title=Forward won't be eligible until second semester|publisher=ESPN|date=July 8, 2003|access-date=July 8, 2003}}</ref> but he averaged a career-best 19.5 points per game and also led the Lobos in rebounding, steals, and blocks as a junior in 2003–04. He became the first Lobos player to lead the team in all those categories in the same season and was awarded the Bob King Team MVP Award. He was the second Lobo in 33 years, and the fifth all-time, to average more than 19 points and nine rebounds for an entire season, joining [[Luc Longley]], [[Willie Long]], [[Mel Daniels]] and [[Ira Harge]]. A First Team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] selection, Granger was twice named the league's Player of the Week for the weeks ending December 22 and January 25.<ref name="nbabio" />

====Senior====
As a senior in 2004–05, Granger was the only player in the NCAA to average at least 18.8 points and 8.9 rebounds per game, while also averaging at least 2.0 blocks, 2.0 steals, and 2.0 assists. He led the team in scoring, rebounding, steals and blocked shots for the second year in a row. He became the first player in school history to record 60+ assists, blocks and steals in a season. In 52 games, he registered 91 career blocked shots, ranking sixth all-time in New Mexico history. He fell just six points short of 1,000 in his New Mexico career, and for the second year in a row, he was given the Bob King Team MVP Award. He was named the [[Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|MWC tournament]] MVP and earned First Team All-Mountain West honors for the second straight year.<ref name="nbabio" /> He was also runner-up to [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]]'s [[Andrew Bogut]] as MWC Player of the Year.<ref name="abqjournal" />

==NBA career==
===Indiana Pacers (2005–2014)===
====Early years (2005–2007)====
Granger was selected 17th overall in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] after averaging 7.5 points and 4.9 rebounds in 78 games. He was a starter in the T-Mobile Rookie Challenge during All-Star Weekend in Houston on February 17, 2006, where he had nine points, three rebounds, two assists and a blocked shot in six minutes, and shot 2-of-4 from 3-point range.<ref name="nbabio" />

In 2006–07, Granger became one of only four Pacers players to hit 100+ 3-point field goals in a season in the previous 15 years. He led Indiana with 110, after making just 30 3-pointers in his rookie season. He was the only Pacers player to see action in all 82 games; he started 57 games, including the first 14 and 42 of the last 44 games.<ref name="nbabio" />

====Perennial team scoring leader (2007–2012)====
In 2007–08, Granger was the team's leading scorer with an average of 19.6 points per game. On November 5, 2007, he was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played Tuesday, October 30 through Sunday, November 4. It was his first and only [[NBA Player of the Week]] honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/granger_pow_071105.html|title=Granger named East Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=November 5, 2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071215230306/http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/granger_pow_071105.html|archive-date=December 15, 2007}}</ref> He set a franchise record by making 65 straight free throws (January 21 to February 22), breaking the record set by [[Reggie Miller]] in 2005.<ref name="nbabio" />

On October 31, 2008, Granger signed a five-year contract extension with the Pacers believed to be worth a guaranteed $60 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/granger_extension_081031.html|title=Granger signs contract extension|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2008|access-date=October 31, 2008}}</ref> The new contract began in 2009–10, with incentives that could have pushed the total closer to $65 million.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stein|first=Marc|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3676045|title=Pacers F Granger signs 5-year extension in $60M range|work=ESPN.com|date=October 31, 2008|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref>

[[File:Danny Granger.jpg|thumb|Granger in December 2008, shooting a free throw]]
In 2008–09, Granger became the first player in NBA history to lift his scoring average at least five points per game in three consecutive seasons, and the first Indiana player to average more than 25 points per game in more than 30 years. He ranked fifth in the NBA with 25.8 points and was named the NBA's [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/2009/news/05/12/most.improved/|title=Pacers' Granger wins Kia Most Improved Player Award|work=NBA.com|date=May 12, 2009|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref> His average was the highest by an Indiana player since [[Billy Knight]]'s single-season team record of 26.6 points per game in 1976–77. Granger scored 20 or more points in a career-high 16 straight games from December 15 to January 19, tying the longest streak in the Pacers' NBA history. In a three-game span from January 3 to 7, he scored 35 or more points in each game and is the only Pacers player to ever do so. In February 2009, he played in his first and only [[NBA All-Star Game]]. He missed a total of 15 games due to injury or illness, including 11 in February and March with a torn tendon in his right foot.<ref name="nbabio" />

In 2009–10, Granger led the Pacers with 24.1 points per game, eighth best in the NBA and third best in the Eastern Conference. He scored 20 or more points in 45 of 62 appearances and scored 30+ points 16 times. He tallied a career-high 44 points against the [[Utah Jazz]] on March 26, 2010. He missed a total of 18 games due to injury or illness, including 16 straight in December and January with a torn plantar fascia in his right foot.<ref name="nbabio" />

In the summer of 2010, Granger won gold as a member of the [[2010 United States men's FIBA World Championship team|US national team]] at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]].

In 2010–11, Granger was the Pacers' leading scorer for the fourth season in a row, with 20.5 points per game, which was 16th best in the NBA and his third consecutive season of 20+ points per game. He scored in double figures in all but four games and tallied 20 or more points 39 times with 30+ points nine times.<ref name="nbabio" /> On January 2, 2011, he grabbed a career-high 17 rebounds in a 98–92 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/rewind_110102.html|title=Game Rewind: Knicks 98, Pacers 92|work=NBA.com|date=January 2, 2011|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref>

[[File:Danny Granger and Luol Deng.jpg|thumb|Granger (#33) in December 2011, attempting to block [[Luol Deng]]'s shot]]
In the lockout-shortened 2011–12 season, Granger was the Pacers' leading scorer for the fifth consecutive season—his 18.7 points per game ranked 22nd best in the NBA.<ref name="nbabio" />

====Injury-riddled end to Pacers tenure (2012–2014)====
Granger missed the first 55 games of the 2012–13 season with tendinosis of the left knee. He played five games between February 23 and March 3 before being placed back on the inactive list and eventually having surgery on the knee on April 4.<ref name="nbabio" />

Granger missed the first 25 games of the 2013–14 season with a strained left calf.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/grangda01/gamelog/2014/|title=Danny Granger 2013-14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref><ref name=pacers-rockets>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489261|title=Pacers crush Rockets to snap 2-game slide|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2013|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref> Indiana fans gave Granger a standing ovation on December 20 when he made his season debut in the first quarter of the Pacers' 114–81 win over the [[Houston Rockets]], and chanted his name when he finally made his first basket, a 3-pointer, early in the fourth.<ref name="pacers-rockets" /> He appeared in 29 games (2 starts) for the Pacers in 2013–14, averaging 8.3 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 22.5 minutes per game.<ref name="nbabio" />

===Los Angeles Clippers (2014)===
On February 20, 2014, Granger was traded, along with a 2015 second-round pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Evan Turner]] and [[Lavoy Allen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140220-granger-trade|title=Sixers Trade Evan Turner and Lavoy Allen to Indiana for Danny Granger and Future Second-round Pick|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2014|access-date=February 20, 2014}}</ref> He was bought out by the 76ers on February 26,<ref>{{cite web|last=Aldridge|first=David|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/02/26/sixers-granger-buyout/|title=Granger, Sixers reach buyout agreement|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2014|access-date=February 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308021307/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/02/26/sixers-granger-buyout/|archive-date=March 8, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Stein|first1=Marc|last2=Shelburne|first2=Ramona|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10522831/philadelphia-76ers-buy-danny-granger|title=Sixers buy out Danny Granger|work=ESPN.com|date=February 26, 2014|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref> and two days later, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-former-all-star-danny-granger|title=CLIPPERS SIGN FORMER ALL-STAR DANNY GRANGER|work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2014|access-date=February 28, 2014}}</ref>

=== Miami Heat (2014–2015) ===
On July 14, 2014, Granger signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-danny-granger|title=HEAT Signs Danny Granger|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2014|access-date=July 14, 2014}}</ref> On February 19, 2015, he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in a three-team trade involving the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-stockpile-draft-picks-trade-heat|title=Suns Stockpile Draft Picks in Trade with Heat|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}}</ref> However, due to knee problems, he did not play for the Suns in 2014–15.<ref>{{cite ==Personal life==
Granger was raised as a member of [[Jehovah's Witnesses]]. Granger's younger brother, [[Scotty Granger|Scotty]], is a musical artist and songwriter. Granger is the great-nephew of the "Queen of Gospel", [[Mahalia Jackson]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Friedell|first=Nick|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/blog/ball_dont_lie/post/One-on-One-Danny-Granger-talks-superheroes-pud?urn=nba,125727|title=One-on-One: Danny Granger talks superheroes, pudding, movies|work=Yahoo.com|date=December 1, 2008|access-date=December 1, 2008}}</ref>

Granger has a wife and three children.<ref name=abqjournal2>{{cite web|last=Grammer|first=Geoff|url=https://www.abqjournal.com/933356/ex-lobo-granger-has-a-happy-homecoming.html|title=Former Lobo Granger at home in the Pit as TV analyst|work=abqjournal.com|date=January 22, 2017|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref>

Granger is actively involved in the "Dribble to Stop Diabetes" campaign due to his family's history with diabetes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/video/channels/nba_tv/2013/01/14/2013011diabetes-grainger.nba|title=Dribble to Stop Diabetes: Danny Granger|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2013|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref>

On the side, toward the end of his playing career, Granger built up a [[real estate]] investment company.<ref>{{cite web|last=Putzier|first=Konrad|url=https://therealdeal.com/2016/06/28/ex-ballers-to-nba-stars-dont-let-real-estate-investors-scam-you/|title=Ex-ballers to NBA stars: Don't let RE investors scam you|work=therealdeal.com|date=June 28, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref>

In January 2017, Granger began working as a studio and game analyst for the [[CBS Sports Network]].<ref name="abqjournal2" />

In April 2017, Granger was inducted into New Mexico Sports Hall of Fame.<ref>{{cite web|last=Chester|first=Jared|url=http://krqe.com/2016/12/17/nm-sports-hall-of-fame-inductees-announced/|title=NM Sports Hall of Fame inductees announced|work=krqe.com|date=December 17, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref>
